text:
mel: quick question — designing validation for the new Console bulk-edit form. thinking about two patterns: inline errors directly under fields vs a persistent error strip at the top that summarizes failures. also debating required field signalling: asterisk-only, explicit “Required” label, or inline hint text. accessibility and mobile/touch have to be first-class.

sam: inline errors for field-level problems — users fix faster. summary strip only for global submit failures (server errors or multiple fields). keep strip but make it a clear anchor link to first error.

li: accessibility notes — if inline errors are used, they need role=alert or aria-live="assertive" and keyboard focus to the first invalid control on submit. summary strip should include an unordered list with links to each field id.

daria: +1 to not relying on hover for required hints. asterisk alone is quick but ambiguous for some users. maybe a hybrid: asterisk + small helper text above the form: “Fields marked * are required”. avoid cluttering every label with the word "Required".

kyle: destructive action confirmations: for bulk-deletes should we use typed-confirm (type the resource name) or a checkbox + CTA? typed-confirm reduces mistakes but poor for power users. proposal: typed-confirm for org-level / irreversible deletes; simple checkbox + secondary confirm for single-item or undoable actions.

mel: microcopy suggestion for confirm flows — want quick feedback.

mel: ```
// confirmation microcopy examples
Primary CTA: Delete workspace
Secondary help: This action permanently deletes all pipelines and logs. This cannot be undone.
Typed confirm placeholder: Type the workspace name to confirm: "acme-prod"
``` 

sam: small nit — CTA color and copy: use verb-first CTAs ("Delete workspace") and keep the cancel as plain text. For the strip summary CTA, show "Fix errors" and focus the first invalid field when clicked.

li: touch accessibility: summary strip should be tappable and expand to reveal errors on narrow screens. avoid tiny hit targets for links inside error items.

daria: can we do a quick poll in the next design review? two variants: (A) inline-only (with a short summary) (B) top-strip-first (strip always visible) — test with 5 internal users and one keyboard-only/a11y tester.

kyle: logging/telemetry idea — capture which pattern leads to submit retries and time-to-success. will help quantify UX cost vs. discoverability.
